notes:
the destination - lean bulk is the vehicle. Deadline advanced after 160x8 on Jul 20 (e1RM ~203). Pace: e1RM 210 by Sep 1, 215 by Oct 1, 220 by Nov 1, 225 by Dec 1. Stretch: 235 by Jan 15, 2027. The risk window is Oct-Dec (historical layoff season).

STATUS 8/28: e1RM 210.0 (175x6,5 on 8/27) - the Sep 1 gate, hit 4 days early. But bench is the ONLY goal at risk. Required rate to Dec 1 is +1.11 e1RM/wk; trailing-21d actual is +1.19/wk, a 7% margin. Squat by contrast runs +6.95/wk against +1.28 required. Bench cannot afford any deceleration.

DIAGNOSIS 8/28: bench stalled because Adam applied a different progression rule than squat. Bench 8/07-8/27 went 165x8,6 -> 165x8,7 -> 170x7,5 -> 175x6,5: +10 lb of bar, +1.0 e1RM. He is buying load with reps ~1:1. Squat over the same window sat on 225 for FOUR sessions (6,6 / 7,6 / 8,6 / 8,7) before jumping to 235, and gained 25 e1RM. Same athlete, same month, same creatine - the rule is the only difference. Precedent: 165 took 17 days to consolidate (6,4 on 7/30 -> 8,7 on 8/16).

PLAN (set 8/28, supersedes ad-hoc load calls):
1. PARK AT 175 until it is 8,7. Do not jump on a session that did not earn it. 175x8,7 = e1RM 221.7 on its own, ~90% of the remaining gap. Expect ~17 days by the 165 precedent, so ~mid-Sep. Then 180 (180x8,7 = 228) clears 225 in early October with two months of buffer.
2. ADD A THIRD WORKING SET. Adam's own 8/23 note: 'the volume problem is bench-specific.' Row gets 3 sets and just hit 175x8,8,7; bench gets 2. Do not change load and set count in the same session - he correctly pushed back on that once already (8/23).
3. HEAVY SINGLES GO AT THE FRONT OF PUSH DAY, BEFORE the working sets - never after, and never as a separate 4th session. Rationale: a single is skill + max CNS effort and needs to be fresh; done after 3x8 it rehearses a broken groove and the number is meaningless for calibration. One single costs the working sets almost nothing in the reverse direction. A 4th day is recovery Adam does not have (HRV 41.0 on 8/27, 2nd-lowest in series) for ~5 min of work.
   Now -> mid-Sep: NO singles. Consolidating 175 is the higher-value job.
   Mid-Sep -> early Oct: open with a top set of 3 @ RPE 8, ~190, then the 6-8 work.
   Oct -> mid-Nov: top SINGLE @ RPE 8-9 before working sets, every push day. Start ~200 and climb. Trim backoff volume as singles get heavy.
   Late Nov: one true attempt, ~2 weeks before the test window so he can recover from it.
   Throughout: RPE 8-9, NOT true maxes. Weekly maxing is how this stalls in October.
4. SPOTTER OR SAFETY PINS mandatory once singles exceed ~190. Adam has never failed a rep in 170 logged sessions because he has never trained below 5 reps - that changes in October. He should know what a miss feels like before it happens under 215.

CAVEAT: e1RM 225 is NOT a tested 225. Every one of 170 logged sessions is 6-8 reps (accessories 10s); Epley off 8-rep sets overestimates true 1RM for a lifter with no heavy-single practice. The rep transition below is the mechanism that closes that gap - start it in September, not November.
Rep progression: rebuild with 6-8 reps, transition primary work toward 4-6 reps in Sep-Oct, 2-4 reps in Nov, controlled heavy singles before the test while retaining backoff volume. Thanksgiving week is the first test window; attempt only after a clean 205x3 or 210x2.

instrumental to bench-225; keep lean-ish. RETARGETED 8/15: scale flat Jul 15-Aug 15 (76.7->76.5kg) on ~2,950 target; empirical TDEE 2,865 (18 logged days/21d window, observed -0.2 lb/wk). New target 3,200 kcal (~TDEE+335, ~0.65 lb/wk ceiling), protein 150-155g in 4+ feedings, fat ~75g, carbs fill. Recompute PUSHED to ~Sep 15 (was Sep 1): creatine started 8/21 (5g/day, see profile.supplements) and its ~1-2 lb water gain lands inside the Sep 1 window, which would inflate the apparent surplus and wrongly trigger a calorie cut. Run the recompute on a window starting ~Sep 5, once water has plateaued; ignore the 8/21-8/23 weigh-ins as trend data. PINNED 8/28 via targetKcalOverride: 3,200 is now enforced in code, not just prose. Before this the served target had already drifted to 3,080 — with the scale flat, empirical TDEE collapses to average logged intake, so every missed/low day ratchets the next day's target down. Remove the override only when deliberately re-targeting. Prior note (Iraki/Morton split) still governs macro shape.

Primary deadline Jan 1, 2027, aligned with reaching ~180 lb on the 0.5 lb/wk lean bulk. Stretch test Dec 1, 2026 only if 285x3 or 295x2 and a clean 305 single are achieved first. Pace by e1RM: regain ~285 by Sep 1, reach ~295 by Oct 1, ~305 by Nov 15, and become 315-ready by Dec 15. Rebuild in the 6-8 rep range, then transition primary work toward 4-6 reps, 2-4 reps, and finally heavy singles while retaining controlled backoff volume.

STATUS 8/29 (legs, 235 repeat as prescribed): 235 x 7,6 — thirteen reps, exactly the thirteen of 8/26 (8,5) redistributed. e1RM 289.8, DOWN from 297.7 on 8/26. Still clears the Sep 1 gate (285) and sits three weeks ahead of the Oct 1 gate (295). Required rate to 315 by Jan 1 is ~1.42 e1RM/wk against a trailing actual far above it — squat is not the goal at risk, bench is.
THE RULE STANDS: 235 was to be repeated until 8,6 or 8,7. It came back 7,6. DO NOT JUMP TO 245 — take 235 a third time and target 8,7. This is the same consolidation shape as bench 165 (7/30: 6,4 -> 8/16: 8,7) and squat 225, which sat for four sessions and then paid 25 e1RM. Two flat sessions at a new load is the normal middle of that, not a stall.
ACCESSORIES 8/29: Calf raises 500 x 8,8,7 (up from 8,8,5 — repeat 500, third set still owes a rep). Unilateral quad extension 140 x 8,8 COMPLETE — goes to 145. Hamstring curl: jumped 135 -> 145, failed at 4, dropped to 140 for 7,5. The prescription was 140 x 3 x 6-8. This is the bench error in a different lift — buying load ahead of the reps, and it cost a whole set (two logged, three prescribed). Next session: 140 for three sets, no 145 until 140 is 8,8,8.
CONTEXT: session moved 15:00 -> 12:45 straight off a phone call, ~80g carbs 1.75h out, HRV 41.0 on 8/27 (2nd-lowest in series). A flat repeat under those conditions is a fueling/recovery reading, not a load reading.
